solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Concern over another pair of cardinals splitting to go separate ways (6,7)

indicatorNotes.splitting: the pair of cardinals splits PART, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to part company = to go separate ways
E and N, two cardinal points of the compass

annotation.surface: A worry about yet another pair of cardinals falling out and going their separate ways.
annotation.walkthrough: The cardinals look like churchmen but are compass points. The definition is cryptic in its own right: a parent company is a business (concern) set over another business.
annotation.definitionFit: A parent company is a business that owns and controls another company.

entries.clue: Cut accommodation for hotel employees? (11)

blocks.note: a butcher's cut of beef, not a reduction
a house for porters, read whimsically

annotation.surface: Hotel staff learning their housing has been cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a reduction in staff housing, but it is a butcher's cut. The question mark flags the made-up reading PORTER HOUSE.
annotation.definitionFit: Porterhouse is a thick steak cut from the short loin.

entries.clue: One who loves Capital Ring (5)

annotation.surface: Someone fond of the Capital Ring, a walking route around London.
annotation.walkthrough: The Capital Ring is a real 78-mile walking trail around London, so the two words look like one name; split them.
annotation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a lover, after Shakespeare's hero.

entries.clue: Void I plug up in high dune (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' turns I FILL over
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed piece goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.high: high = intoxicated, so DUNE is scrambled

blocks.note: DUNE scrambled, split around the middle piece

annotation.surface: Someone stuffing a hollow in a tall sand dune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Void' sounds like the hole being plugged, but it is the definition, used as a verb meaning cancelled.
annotation.definitionFit: To void a contract is to nullify it; void as a past participle means nullified.

entries.clue: Work’s left two duplicates low perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.left two: only the two leftmost letters of the work remain

blocks.note: CYCLE (a work, as in a song cycle), first two letters

annotation.surface: A job's leftovers include two copies of something shabby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective but is a weather-forecast noun: an area of low pressure, of which a cyclone is one example, hence 'perhaps'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a system of low atmospheric pressure, so it is one kind of low.

entries.clue: Compulsory payment initially made under lower court (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of each of the words before 'court'

blocks.note: first letters of Made, Under, Lower
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A fine imposed by a lower court.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a legal ruling, which suits the answer; 'initially' reaches back over three words, not just one.
annotation.definitionFit: A mulct is a fine, a payment imposed as a penalty.

entries.clue: Rocky Marciano imbibing energy drink (9)

indicatorNotes.Rocky: rocky = unsteady, so MARCIANO is scrambled
indicatorNotes.imbibing: the scrambled name takes E inside it

annotation.surface: The boxer Rocky Marciano downing an energy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocky Marciano was a real heavyweight champion, so 'Rocky' reads as his first name; here it is the signal to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso diluted with hot water.

entries.clue: Hooligan having my backing? (3)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, BOY turns into YOB

blocks.note: 'boy!' and 'my!' are both cries of surprise

annotation.surface: A thug who has my support.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, as in 'my, that's big', and so is 'boy!'. YOB, British slang for a lout, is famously 'boy' spelt backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A yob is a rowdy, aggressive young man.

entries.clue: Disapproving of page limit (4)

blocks.note: a rim is an edge or limit

annotation.surface: Someone frowning at a page limit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' is only a link here; read 'Disapproving' on its own as the definition, an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly proper and quick to disapprove.

entries.clue: Fans won’t go far for this weight-watcher’s cheese? (5,5)

annotation.definition: Fans won’t go far for this

blocks.clueFragment: Fans won’t go far for this
blocks.note: a match between neighbouring teams, so the away fans barely travel

annotation.surface: A dieter's cheese so good that people won't travel far for it.
annotation.walkthrough: A local derby is a football match between two nearby clubs. Derby is also a mild English cheese, so a slimmer might want a 'lo-cal' one.
annotation.definitionFit: Supporters at a local derby need travel only a short way to the away ground.

entries.clue: Ripon excited about green cheese (8)

indicatorNotes.excited: stirred up, so RIPON's letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.about: the scrambled letters go round ECO

blocks.note: RIPON rearranged, split around the middle

annotation.surface: The people of Ripon, a Yorkshire cathedral city, getting worked up about a mouldy cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green cheese' looks like one thing, mould or the moon, but 'green' belongs to the wordplay. Ripon is a small city in North Yorkshire.
annotation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from ewe's milk.

entries.clue: Jerk beginning to trouble charming woman (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take just the first letter of 'trouble'

annotation.surface: A cad starting to bother an attractive woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a man and 'charming' like a compliment; one is a sudden movement and the other means spell-casting.
annotation.definitionFit: A twitch is a small sudden jerk of a muscle.

entries.clue: What borders run with annoyance south of Orpington? (7,4)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, W + IRE sits below CHICKEN

blocks.note: the Orpington is a breed of chicken

annotation.surface: Someone asking what makes people in the Kent town of Orpington annoyed.
annotation.walkthrough: Orpington is a town in south-east London, but also the chicken breed named after it. 'Run' here is a chicken run, the fenced pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Chicken wire is light wire mesh used to fence in a chicken run.

entries.clue: Rough nature of cold bitter’s characteristic? (10)

blocks.note: bitter, the British beer, is characteristically hoppy

annotation.surface: Asking whether a cold pint of bitter has a rough edge.
annotation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of ale flavoured with hops; the question mark covers the invented noun HOPPINESS.
annotation.definitionFit: Choppiness is the roughness of water broken into short waves.

entries.clue: Perhaps shares part of spoil of trophies brought back (9)

annotation.definitionNote: a portfolio holds shares; 'perhaps shares' is a definition by example

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters inside spOIL OF TROPhies

annotation.surface: A share of the spoils of war carried home as trophies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shares' looks like a verb about dividing loot, but it means stocks, which an investor holds in a portfolio.
annotation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a collection of investments, such as shares.

entries.clue: Thus expert studied baker’s product (4,5)

blocks.note: a dab hand is an expert
to read a subject is to study it

annotation.surface: A skilled baker has studied the craft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dab' for an expert comes from the British phrase 'dab hand'.
annotation.definitionFit: Soda bread is bread raised with bicarbonate of soda rather than yeast.

entries.clue: First-class artist’s returning strain (4)

indicatorNotes.returning: coming back, so AI + RA is read backwards

blocks.note: A1, first-class, written with I for 1

annotation.surface: A top artist returning to work after an injury strain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like an injury, but it is a musical tune.
annotation.definitionFit: A strain is a piece of melody, and an aria is a solo song in opera.

entries.clue: Drill donkey endlessly (4)

blocks.note: BURRO, a small donkey, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Training a donkey without let-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drill' reads as training, but it is the dentist's tool. A burro is a small Spanish donkey.
annotation.definitionFit: A burr is a small rotary drill bit, as used by dentists.

entries.clue: Top arrangement of security devices following anxiety (10)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so LOCKS is placed behind DREAD

annotation.surface: A household's best lock set-up installed after a scare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top' is the head, so 'top arrangement' is a hairstyle; the locks are also hair, which makes the surface pun twice.
annotation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are hair twisted into rope-like strands, a way to arrange what is on top.

entries.clue: Former noble that is supported by king (7)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue, R sits beneath

annotation.surface: A one-time aristocrat kept afloat by the monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former noble' looks like one phrase for an ex-lord; 'Former' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Former and earlier both mean coming before in time.

entries.clue: Charge in bar reversed increase (4,2)

indicatorNotes.in: a charge 'in' a bar is held within it, so FEE sits inside PUB
indicatorNotes.reversed: turned the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

annotation.surface: A pub's charges going up and then back down.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole unit reverses, so FEE comes out as EEF and PUB as B...UP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrasal verb means to add bulk or strength, as muscle is added to a body.

entries.clue: I’m avoiding insurmountable difficulty on the way out (5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: IM is kept out of the word

annotation.surface: Someone escaping a hopeless situation just as they leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the way out' reads as an exit, but it means going out of fashion.
annotation.definitionFit: Passé means outdated, going out of style.

entries.clue: Ruddy copper interrupting rugby tie (8)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so CU breaks into BIND

annotation.surface: A red-faced policeman breaking up a rugby match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the policeman in the surface and the metal in the wordplay; 'tie' is a verb, not a fixture.
annotation.definitionFit: Rubicund means ruddy, reddish in complexion.

entries.clue: Go up first to Conservative member (5)

annotation.surface: Rising to become the first Conservative MP.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' sounds parliamentary next to 'Conservative', but it means an arm or leg.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: climbing is ascending, whether a hill, a ladder or a ranking.

entries.clue: I left this out, cutting long material, characteristically? (10)

annotation.definitionNote: used adjectivally: philistine = materialistic and uncultured

indicatorNotes.out: out = in disarray, so I, L and THIS are scrambled
indicatorNotes.cutting: the scrambled letters cut into PINE

blocks.note: to long for is to pine

annotation.surface: An editor admitting they left a passage out while trimming a long text.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' is an adjective here: a philistine characteristically values material things over culture. The question mark flags the loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A philistine is hostile to art and culture, caring only for material things.

entries.clue: Goblin took a bite out of Frodo? (3)

indicatorNotes.took a bite out of: taking a bite out of something removes a piece, here the letters BIT

blocks.note: Frodo Baggins is Tolkien's best-known hobbit
a bit, a small bite, taken away

annotation.surface: A goblin biting a chunk out of Frodo.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Frodo as one example of a hobbit.
annotation.definitionFit: A hob is a sprite or goblin in English folklore.

entries.clue: Bird again on island (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, BIS is placed after I

blocks.note: bis, Latin for twice, is a musical direction to repeat

annotation.surface: A bird back on its island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Again' is BIS, the direction in a musical score to play a passage twice; it is less familiar than the island's I.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

entries.clue: Wild black British Airedale dog not staying around? (13)

indicatorNotes.Wild: wild = unruly, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A wild black Airedale terrier that won't stay put.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not staying around' reads as a runaway dog, but it means breaking down and disappearing.
annotation.definitionFit: Biodegradable material decays naturally rather than persisting in the environment.
